rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī, via Ibn Isḥāq and unnamed scholars of earlier scripture, transmits an account of Adam and Eve, the brothers’ offerings, Cain killing Abel, and Cain’s curse and punishment.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي عن ابن إسحاق عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After one offering is rejected and the other accepted, Cain’s anger and envy lead him to threaten his brother with murder.
rows.anchor: أي لأخيه الذي قبل قربانه حسدا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those deeply characterized by piety are accepted; they do not persist in sins, whether idolatry or otherwise.
rows.anchor: فلا معصية لهم يصرون عليها بشرك ولا غيره

words: فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلْءَاخَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejected offering reflects Cain’s own state, not Abel’s; killing Abel only distances Cain further from the rank he envies.
rows.anchor: فعدم تقبل قربانك من نفسك لا مني

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel first admonishes Cain, then explains that fear of God restrains him from defending himself lest resistance carry him beyond permitted bounds; Cain is sinful, not an idolater.
rows.anchor: أعلمه ثانيا أن الخوف من الله منعه من أن يمانعه عن نفسه ملينا لقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel frames his grave assertion with an emphatic conditional oath because such a serious statement is difficult to believe.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا بالقسم لأن مثل ما يخبر به عظيم لا يكاد يصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic negation and fronted object generalize his refusal; the nominal construction avoids asserting certainty about his future conduct, as an act of reverence toward God.
rows.anchor: وقدم المفعول به تعميما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel’s fear means recalling God’s perfection; calling Him Lord of the worlds recalls His beneficence in creating and nurturing, so Abel will not destroy what God built.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفه بالإحسان إلى خلقه ليكون ذلك مانعا له من الإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares Abel’s refusal to resist with ʿUthmān’s similar conduct.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما فعل عثمان رضي الله عنه

words: إني أريد أن تبوأ بإثمي وإثمك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those near God, the will follows God’s will: they approve obedience, but when sin is divinely willed they accept the decree without approving the sinful act.
rows.anchor: وإن كان معصية أراده من حيث إنه مراد الله ولم يرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests Abel may have been shown that God’s prior knowledge had already decreed that Cain would kill him, helping explain his nonresistance.
rows.anchor: وكأنه من الممكن القريب أن يكون هابيل قد كشف له عن أنه سبق في علم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain would bear the sin and punishment for killing Abel along with his earlier sins; if unable to repay Abel’s right with good deeds, Cain incurs an equivalent share of Abel’s misdeeds.
rows.anchor: إنه يطرح عليك من سيئاتي بمقدار ما عليك من حقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel says he will gain both his own reward and the reward earned by submitting to Cain and withholding his hand.
rows.anchor: وأفوز أنا بأجري وأجرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain’s unjust murder makes him one of the people of Hell, while Abel’s virtuous forbearance earns him Paradise; God can grant victory to the survivor after a martyr’s death.
rows.anchor: وأكون أنا من أصحاب الجنة جزاء لي بإحساني في إيثار حياتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Abel’s warning should have led Cain to obey and avoid sin, Cain’s hardened heart instead turns it into a motive for murder.
rows.anchor: هذا الوعظ جديرا بأن يكون سببا لطاعته وزاجرا له عن معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form signals that the sanctity and awe of murder made Cain’s soul require a strenuous process to make the act seem easy.
rows.anchor: إذ القتل لما جعل الله له من الحرمة وكساه من الهيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain’s soul treated him with specious rationalizations, emboldened him, and overcame his reason; one who imagines a sin’s punishment normally resists it, but a dominated person yields to his soul.
rows.anchor: حتى غلبت على عقله فانطاع لها وانقاد فأقدم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killing follows from the soul’s enticement, and loss follows from the murder.
rows.anchor: وسبب عن القتل قوله : { فأصبح }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning is named because it is a time when relief is expected, but becoming a loser describes Cain at every time.
rows.anchor: لأن الصباح محل توقع الارتياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain loses through God’s anger at his assault on God’s creation and through the anger of his fellow humans at his attack on one of their kind.
rows.anchor: وغضب أبناء جنسه عليه لاجترائه على أحدهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Cain did not know how to kill; Satan demonstrated by smashing a bird’s head with a stone, and Cain copied him while Abel slept.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه لم يدر كيف يقتله

words: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Cain did not know what to do with the body, being the first death with burial still unknown, God sends a raven to teach him.
rows.anchor: إذ كان أول ميت فلم يكن الدفن معروفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Searching means turning over and loosening the compact soil to make an empty space; the raven searches to bury another raven that died.
rows.anchor: البحث وهو التفتيش في التراب بتليين ما تراص منه وإزاحته من مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden subject of ‘show him’ can be God or the raven; the author prefers the raven as subject because this exposes Cain’s ignorance and the bird’s greater knowledge and goodness.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لتوقيفه على عجزه وجهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A corpse becomes wholly something that must be covered, and nakedness requires concealment.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت السوءة واجبة الستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised believers fear no blame for condemning wrong; they exert their power to humble enemies and support allies, unlike hypocrites who fear Jewish allies’ censure and avoid harming them.
rows.anchor: يفعلون في الجهاد في ذلك جميع ما تصل قدرتهم وتبلغ قوتهم إليه من إنكال الأعداء وإهانتهم

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These exalted traits are God’s gift, since God creates all human actions and grants generously to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: أي الله لأنه خالق لجميع أفعال العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s vastness means His perfection and giving have no limit; His knowledge encompasses who deserves good and all that can be known.
rows.anchor: فهو يعطي من سعة ليس لها حد ولا يلحقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the preceding passage negated the disbelievers’ allegiance as love, aid, and closeness, it concludes that true allegiance is exclusively God’s and His allies’.
rows.anchor: ولما نفى سبحانه ولايتهم بمعنى المحبة وبمعنى النصرة وبمعنى القرب بكل اعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is truly able to do what a protecting ally must do; everyone else can act only through Him.
rows.anchor: ولا يقدر غيره على شيء من ذلك إلا به سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s own allegiance is known through the allegiance of His allies; the Messenger is named first as the most deserving, and attachment to God marks his exalted rank.
rows.anchor: من تعرف ولايته سبحانه بولايتهم بادئا بأحقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer establishes connection with the Creator, while almsgiving is beneficence toward created beings.
rows.anchor: أي تمكينا لوصلتهم بالخالق { ويؤتون الزكاة } إحسانا إلى الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing coordinates ‘while bowing’ with establishing prayer, describing believers who bow; the author notes Jews and Christians do not bow in prayer.
rows.anchor: أي ويكونون من أهل الركوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘while bowing’ is a circumstantial clause describing the person giving alms.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون حالا من فاعل الإيتاء

rows.speaker: أسباب النزول
rows.claim: A report on the occasion says the verse was revealed about ʿAlī, who gave his ring to a petitioner while bowing.
rows.anchor: أنها نزلت في علي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is plural despite the single reported occasion to encourage others to emulate the good deed promptly and prevent treating it as exclusive to ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: وجمع وإن كان السبب واحدا ترغيبا في مثل فعله نم فعل الخير والتعجيل به

words: وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding implication is that those allying with others join Satan’s party and lose; this verse states the converse, allegiance to God, His Messenger, and believers.
rows.anchor: وحزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To ally with God is to strive to be allied to the One who possesses all sources of might.
rows.anchor: يجتهد في ولاية الذي له مجامع العز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The allies are named again for blessing and to state the intended referents explicitly; the Messenger is described as one formed by the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وأعاد ذكر من خص الولاية بهم تبركا بأسمائهم وتصريحا بالمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of leaving the understood predicate ‘they are victorious,’ the verse names God’s party to honor and encourage them to choose His allegiance.
rows.anchor: ولكنه أظهر ما شرفهم به ترغيبا لهم في ولايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s party is the group gathered around what pleases the Supreme King, including what has been made hard for them; they alone prevail, while opponents are defeated and gathered for Hell.
rows.anchor: القوم الذين يجمعهم على ما يرضي الملك الأعلى ما حزبهم أي اشتد عليهم فيه

words: لَا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ دِينَكُمْ هُزُوًۭا وَلَعِبًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage has explained why disbelievers must not be allied with and restricted allegiance to God, it now warns of further reasons for disavowing them.
rows.anchor: نبه سبحانه على العلل المانعة من ولاية الكفار وحصر الولاية فيه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form of ‘adopt’ suggests that anyone allying with mockers must struggle against reason and follow desire.
rows.anchor: ونبه بصيغة الافتعال على أن من يوالهم يجاهد عقله على ذلك اتباعا لهواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture recipients before the Muslims mocked the religion knowingly and stubbornly after recognizing its truth.
rows.anchor: يعني أنهم فعلوا الهزو عنادا بعد تحققهم صحة الدين

words: مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning that the scripture was given before the Muslims reflects how time affects obedience and disobedience; the earlier grant did not span all previous time.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تطاول الزمان له تأثير فيما عليه الإنسان من طاعة أو عصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general prohibition also includes idol-worshipping polytheists, who lack transmitted prophetic knowledge and conceal evidence clear to reason, as well as others whether or not their mockery is known.
rows.anchor: الذين لا علم لهم نقل عن الأنبياء

rows.speaker: البصريون والكسائي
rows.claim: Basran readers and al-Kisāʾī read ‘allies’ in the accusative; the author invokes the other reading to indicate that the prohibition applies whether or not mockery is known.
rows.anchor: غير قراءة البصريين والكسائي بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture adherents and polytheists are united in envy and contempt for Muslims, so Muslims should never ally with them.
rows.anchor: فلا تصح لكم موالاتهم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allying with another makes one God’s enemy, whose destruction is irreparable; established faith requires fearing God by obeying this prohibition, and without that fear there is no faith.
rows.anchor: ومن عاداه هلك هلاكا لا يضار معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call can mean some Muslims summon the rest to a gathering and they eagerly respond, or the caller speaks aloud as if addressing an assembly and they answer in action.
rows.anchor: إلى الإقبال إلى الندى وهو المجتمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse expresses the destination as the prayer call’s gathering; mockers deliberately laugh and jeer, saying the Muslims bray like donkeys.
rows.anchor: فيتعمدون الضحك والسخرية ويقولون : صاحوا كصياح العير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockery reflects lack of reason: even considering purification, worldly detachment, recitation, and humility before the King of kings shows prayer’s beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: بمجرده كاف في اعتقاد حسنها وجلالها وهيبتها وكمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to prayer has secrets beyond thought; its nineteen words are said to ward off the nineteen keepers of Hell from its reciter.
rows.anchor: تسع عشرة كلمة , ليكف الله به عن قائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleven words of the iqāma are hoped to make its adherent a companion of the eleven: the ten promised Paradise and their pivot, the Prophet, pivot of all existence.
rows.anchor: وجعلت الإقامة إحدى عشرة كلمة رجاء أن يكون معتقدها رفيقا لأحد عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call gathers the religion’s roots and branches; the author says he detailed its secrets in his book on the testimony and call to prayer.
rows.anchor: ( الإيذان بفتح أسرار التشهد والأذان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context answers deniers who thought the dead neither sensed anything nor understood speech: angels seize them, none can prevent it, and the angels at the surah’s beginning signal a final judgment without delay.
rows.anchor: الذين أخبرناكم أول السورة أنهم إذا أبصروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrival before God displays His overwhelming majesty, through the death that decisively demonstrates His complete knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: ملا لنا من العظمة بالموت الذي هو دال على شمول علمنا وتمام قدرتنا قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come separately, no one accompanying another, and stripped of every attachment that had kept them from following the messengers.
rows.anchor: ليس أحد منكم مع أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They return as isolated, weak, and poor as at their first creation, exposing the emptiness of the worldly gathering in which they took pride.
rows.anchor: فأين جمعكم الذي كنتم به تستكبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God granted was wealth and the ability to manage it as a blessing for seeking His pleasure; they instead treated it as intrinsically theirs and turned from Him.
rows.anchor: ملكناكم من المال ومكناكم من إصلاحه نعمة عليكم لتتوصلوا به إلى رضانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They left their wealth behind, so it cannot help them or preserve the status they once claimed through it.
rows.anchor: فما أغنى عنكم ما كنتم منه تستكبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hoped their idols would intercede, mockingly or in this world or—if resurrection is granted—in the next; God taunts them by demanding to see the absent intercessors.
rows.anchor: على تقدير التسليم لصحة البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They falsely claimed idols shared God’s authority over them, worshipping the idols in ease and invoking them in hardship; no screen can conceal them from God.
rows.anchor: أن لهم فيكم نصيبا مع الله حتى كنتم تعبدونهم في وقت الرخاء وتدعونه في وقت الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase introduces the terrified unbelievers’ bewildered and helpless response, marked by confusion, shock, and humiliation.
rows.anchor: دل على بهتهم في جواب هذا الكلام الهائل المرعب حيرة وعجزا ودهشا وذلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Between you’ usually signals presence or nearness; its severance here is so complete that even the thought of former connection vanishes, leaving no path of contact.
rows.anchor: ذكر البين في شيء يدل على قربه في الجملة وحضوره ولو في الذهن

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: The majority read the word in the nominative, while Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative as an adverbial expression; the meaning remains severed connection.
rows.anchor: قراءة نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connection’s end stems from the disappearance of what they relied on; everything they falsely claimed has gone and become void.
rows.anchor: وهو زوال المستند الذي كانوا يستندون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving divine unity, prophethood, and the efficacy of God’s command, the passage turns the listener to ponder fresh signs, including the earlier proofs and Abraham’s argument, to know God’s essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: ولما ثبتت الوحدانية والنبوة والرسالة وتقاريع من تقاريعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits seeds into crops and plants; emergence from nonexistence is figuratively a splitting of the imagined darkness of nothingness.
rows.anchor: وعبر بذلك لأن الشيء قبل وجوده كان معدوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kernel inside edible fruit is split to produce trees, though it is not itself the end sought; its subtle wisdoms point to the perfect, singular Creator.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون مقصودا لذاته بفلقها عن الأشجار

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s account observes a seed splitting in moist soil and sending a shoot upward and roots downward.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الرازي ما حاصله : إن النواة والحبة تكون

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī identifies the seed as the connecting cause joining the tree that rises above ground and the roots descending below.
rows.anchor: وتلك الحبة أو النواة سبب واصل بين الشجرتين

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: A tiny seed develops into a tree with varied substances and successive branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit, demonstrating the power of the freely choosing Creator.
rows.anchor: إذا تأملت ظهور شجرة من نواة صغيرة

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Walnuts and almonds have four layers of covering around the intended kernel; the varied textures and products of one tree exceed what uniform natural causes explain.
rows.anchor: فتولد هذه الأجسام المختلفة طبعا وصفة ولونا وشكلا وطعما مع تساوي تأثيرات الطبائع

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Fruits combine contrasting qualities, and their useful parts occupy different positions: the edible core may be inside, outside, absent, or encompass the whole fruit; this variety indicates a choosing Creator.
rows.anchor: واختلاف هذه الطبائع والأحوال المتضادة والخواص المتنافرة حتى في الحبة الواحدة لا يكون عن طبيعة

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Seeds differ in color and shape, each type has its own benefit, and a fruit may feed one animal but poison another; shared natural and celestial influences cannot account for this.
rows.anchor: في كل نوع منها خاصية ومنفعة غير ما في الآخر

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Leaf veins branch into ever finer channels like spinal nerves, drawing fine earthly particles through narrow passages and revealing meticulous care in the design of a tree.
rows.anchor: وعن كل واحد منها خيوط أخرى أدق من الأولى

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: The hierarchy of care rises from tree to plants, animals, and humans; plants and animals serve human bodily needs, while the body serves knowledge, love, and worship of God.
rows.anchor: إنما خلق الحيوان والنبات في هذا العالم ليكون غذاء ودواء

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Contemplating a leaf and tracing its order upward through the tree and beyond leads toward the ultimate purpose of knowledge and love in human souls and opens endless disclosures.
rows.anchor: فسبيلك أن تنظر في ورقة الشجرة وتتأمل في تلك الأوتار ثم تترقى منها
